title: Anaheim: Architecture and Algorithms for Processing Fully Homomorphic Encryption in Memory
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) workloads on GPUs are bottlenecked not by NTT (number-theoretic transform) computation but by simple element-wise modular arithmetic operations that saturate off-chip DRAM bandwidth, preventing GPUs from being practical FHE accelerators despite their computational resources.
method: Anaheim is a PIM (processing-in-memory) architecture for FHE that augments DRAM with versatile PIM units supporting modular integer arithmetic instructions (addition, multiplication, NTT butterfly, etc.) to execute element-wise operations in-memory, eliminating the off-chip bandwidth bottleneck. The design includes optimized FHE execution flows that partition computation between GPU (NTT-heavy phases) and PIM units (element-wise phases), efficient data mapping algorithms that exploit DRAM's internal structure (bank/row organization) to minimize data movement overhead within DRAM, and an end-to-end software framework for GPU-PIM co-execution.

title: PreDAC: An Efficient Framework of Pre-Refining Enhanced Design Space Exploration for Approximate Computing
problem: Design Space Exploration (DSE) algorithms for approximate computing face challenges obtaining optimal solutions within large and complex design spaces efficiently.
method: Introduces pre-refining enhanced DSE framework that provides customized design space reduction and cost-performance formula specific to each application. Pre-refinement step reduces design space size before DSE, enabling faster convergence. Also proposes innovative cost-performance-based DSE algorithm that leverages pre-refined space.

title: EDA: Energy-Efficient Inter-Layer Model Compilation for Edge DNN Inference Acceleration
problem: Inter-layer operator scheduling on edge NPUs can reduce DRAM traffic by reusing layer outputs in on-chip SRAM, but naive deep traversal of DNN operator graphs greatly increases off-chip memory transactions when on-chip SRAM is small, negating energy savings.
method: EDA is a DNN compilation framework that first transforms the DNN model into a tensor-splitting model and decomposes the model graph into subgraphs. An inter-layer cost model rapidly determines the optimal operator traversal depth for each subgraph given the available on-chip SRAM. EDA then manages the on-chip shared memory space to prevent overflow, and applies operator grouping to improve MAC unit and SRAM space utilization. The resulting compilation avoids both excessive DRAM traffic (from too-deep traversal) and under-utilization (from too-shallow traversal).

title: Veritas - Demystifying Silent Data Corruptions: uArch-Level Modeling and Fleet Data of Modern x86 CPUs
problem: Silent Data Corruptions (SDCs) caused by silicon defects in arithmetic units (integer and FP units) of modern x86 CPUs are poorly characterized at the microarchitecture level; no public data exists on SDC incident rates across CPU microarchitectures or workloads at fleet scale.
method: A full-system gem5-based fault injector models hardware faults in arithmetic units (integer and floating-point) of five modern x86 microarchitectures. Fault injection experiments measure SDC probability and rates across arithmetic unit types and instruction classes. Real-world defect rate data from large-scale datacenter experiments is integrated with the simulation model to estimate SDC incident rates in deployed fleets.

title: Hybe: GPU-NPU Hybrid System for Efficient LLM Inference with Million-Token Context Window
problem: LLM inference with million-token context windows is infeasible on GPUs alone because KV cache activation memory for long contexts (>100K tokens) exceeds total GPU DRAM capacity, making batching impractical and leaving GPU compute cores severely underutilized during the memory-bandwidth-bound decode stage. The compute-memory imbalance between compute-intensive prefill and memory-intensive decode cannot be addressed by batching when KV data dominates physical memory.
method: Hybe assigns the compute-intensive prefill stage to existing high-throughput GPUs (NVIDIA H100 with vLLM) and offloads the memory-bandwidth-bound decode stage to lightweight NPUs sized with exactly enough compute to saturate their HBM bandwidth. The key mechanism is fine-grained KV transmission: as the GPU produces partial KV activations during prefill, it immediately streams them to NPU HBM over interconnect, reducing peak GPU memory footprint dramatically. A stage-wise pipeline scheduler dynamically assigns incoming requests to idle GPU or NPU hardware, minimizing pipeline stalls across the two-stage heterogeneous system. Hybe NPU is implemented in 4nm process with HBM matching the H100 HBM specification.

title: AccelES: Accelerating Top-K SpMV for Embedding Similarity via Low-bit Pruning
problem: Top-K sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) for recommendation system embedding similarity suffers from high latency due to inefficient memory access patterns when scanning full-precision sparse matrices to identify the most relevant embeddings.
method: AccelES employs a two-stage computation scheme: Stage 1 uses a compact low-bit (pruned) representation of the sparse matrix to rapidly identify the top-K candidate entries with minimal data movement, and Stage 2 performs full-precision SpMV only on this pruned candidate subset. Two novel sparse matrix storage formats, Ultra-CSR and Random-CSR, are introduced to optimize memory bandwidth utilization for irregular access patterns inherent in SpMV. The low-bit approximation in Stage 1 filters out irrelevant entries early, reducing the volume of full-precision computation dramatically.

title: Move Less, Retrieve Fast: A Retrieval-in-Memory Architecture for Language Models
problem: Retrieval-augmented language models (RALMs) suffer from substantial data movement and irregular access patterns during retrieval, limiting efficiency on conventional CPU/GPU architectures.
method: Rimast architecture combines 3D-stacked processing-in-memory (PIM) hardware with hardware-software co-design. Hierarchical PIM dataflow minimizes data transfer between memory and compute. Software layers include skew-free data mapping for uniform distribution and adaptive offloading strategies to handle irregular access patterns in RALM retrieval.

title: The Importance of Generalizability in Machine Learning for Systems
problem: ML models deployed in cloud system management tasks frequently encounter out-of-distribution (OOD) data — workloads or resource demand patterns not represented in training data — causing silent mispredictions that degrade server resource balance without any indication of model unreliability.
method: The paper analyzes several ML models used for resource balance in Google's production fleet, empirically demonstrating OOD failure modes. It evaluates multiple OOD detection techniques (distance-based, confidence-based, ensemble methods) and quantifies their trade-offs in precision, recall, and inference overhead. It then demonstrates that Bayesian models — which produce calibrated uncertainty estimates over their outputs — can effectively flag low-confidence predictions to a human operator or fallback policy, improving reliability of ML-driven resource balancing.

title: throttLL'eM: Predictive GPU Throttling for Energy Efficient LLM Inference Serving
problem: LLM inference serving on GPUs consumes excessive energy while providers must simultaneously satisfy Service-Level Objectives (SLOs); static GPU frequency settings over-provision compute resources when request load is low or KV cache pressure is manageable.
method: throttLL'eM uses instance sizing and GPU frequency scaling guided by an ML model that predicts future KV cache usage and batch size. The ML model receives projections of these metrics as inputs and outputs per-iteration performance estimates, enabling iteration-level frequency decisions. The R^2 score exceeds 0.97 and misprediction is under 1 iteration/second on average. Frequency scaling and instance count adjustments are applied jointly to reduce energy while keeping within SLO bounds.

title: PastATPG: A Hybrid ATPG Framework for Better Test Compaction with Partial Assignment SAT
problem: SAT-based ATPG generates complete assignments for all primary inputs in fanin cone, leading to pattern inflation and excessive runtime; test compaction becomes intractable as circuits grow.
method: PA-MiniSat SAT solver enabling partial assignments instead of complete assignments; full-literal watching technique and circuit-adapted branching heuristics; hybrid ATPG framework tightly integrating structural algorithms with PA-MiniSat.

title: Using Analytical Performance/Power Model and Fine-Grained DVFS to Enhance AI Accelerator Energy Efficiency
problem: DVFS on AI processors has historically been applied at coarse granularity (entire program or sub-phases) because the control latency of DVFS mechanisms exceeds the duration of individual AI operators, leaving per-operator energy optimization unexploited. This coarse-grained DVFS fails to match voltage/frequency to the actual compute intensity of each AI operator.
method: The paper proposes an analytical performance/power model that characterizes the compute- and memory-boundedness of individual AI operators, enabling prediction of which operators tolerate voltage/frequency reduction without performance loss. Combined with a hardware mechanism to reduce DVFS control latency, the system applies fine-grained DVFS at the AI-operator level: memory-bound operators run at lower frequency while compute-bound operators run at peak frequency, minimizing energy waste during memory-stall phases.

title: DuQTTA: Dual Quantized Tensor-Train Adaptation with Decoupling Magnitude-Direction for Efficient Fine-Tuning of LLMs
problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for LLMs struggle to balance accuracy and efficiency at scale, particularly when targeting deployment on resource-constrained edge devices with severe memory and compute limitations.
method: DuQTTA combines Tensor-Train decomposition with dual-stage quantization and adaptive optimization strategy with decoupled magnitude-direction updates to minimize model size, achieving up to 65x compression on LLaMA2-7B while improving over LoRA through architectural co-design for edge deployment.

title: Delinquent Loop Pre-execution Using Predicated Helper Threads
problem: Helper-thread branch pre-execution fails when delinquent branches are control-dependent on other delinquent branches: prior work must branch-predict the first delinquent branch (b1) in the helper thread to decide whether to pre-execute the second (b2), merely shifting the misprediction bottleneck to the helper thread. Additionally, stores that both influence a delinquent branch and are control-dependent on it create a disambiguation problem in helper threads.
method: Phelps (Predicated Helper Threads) constructs a helper thread for each inner loop containing delinquent branches and unconditionally pre-executes all delinquent branches (including control-dependent ones) in every loop iteration. Per-branch queues are managed in lockstep with loop iterations, so the main thread can correctly consume or ignore b2 outcomes based on b1 results. Influential stores that are control-dependent on delinquent branches are predicated on those branch outcomes in the helper thread. A dual decoupled helper thread scheme handles outer-inner loop pairs with short/unpredictable inner-loop trip counts.

title: Gaze into the Pattern: Characterizing Spatial Patterns with Internal Temporal Correlations for Hardware Prefetching
problem: Existing spatial-region hardware prefetchers predict memory access footprints using system-level context features (trigger PC, data address) that fail to capture the intrinsic characteristics of spatial access patterns, resulting in poor flexibility and suboptimal prefetch accuracy across diverse workloads.
method: Gaze extracts footprint-internal temporal correlations — the ordering and timing relationships among cache line accesses within a spatial region — as the primary feature for characterizing and predicting spatial access patterns. This avoids dependence on trigger PC or address-based context lookup. For spatial streaming patterns (very high access density within a region), Gaze applies a dedicated two-stage prefetch approach to suppress over-prefetching: a first stage filters high-density streaming footprints and a second stage applies targeted prefetch decisions to avoid redundant prefetches.

title: In-Storage Acceleration of Retrieval Augmented Generation as a Service
problem: As RAG deployments shift knowledge bases to persistent NVMe storage to handle ever-growing corpora, the Search & Retrieval phase — comprising embedding model inference, similarity/relevance search over dynamic data structures, and long-latency storage accesses — becomes the dominant bottleneck for end-to-end latency.
method: The paper proposes a metamorphic in-storage accelerator architecture embedded within NVMe storage devices. The in-storage accelerator is programmable to support diverse RAG retrieval algorithms, dynamic data structures (e.g., HNSW, IVF), and varying computational patterns. It executes smaller language models for query embedding generation entirely in-storage, while the final LLM generation runs on DGX A100 systems. The metamorphic design adapts its functional units to the retrieval algorithm at hand without requiring host CPU involvement in the hot path.

title: COMET: Towards Practical W4A4KV4 LLMs Serving
problem: Prevalent LLM quantization methods (W8A8 or W4-only) do not fully utilize INT4 tensor cores on modern GPUs and cannot reduce the KV cache memory bottleneck, because quantizing activations to 4-bit causes unacceptable accuracy loss with standard methods, leaving W4A4 impractical.
method: COMET introduces a fine-grained mixed-precision quantization algorithm (FMPQ) that compresses most activations to 4-bit while preserving accuracy by identifying and retaining outlier activations at higher precision (e.g., 8-bit) in a mixed-precision format. On the hardware side, COMET develops a highly optimized W4Ax GPU kernel (supporting both W4A4 and W4A8 mixed-precision GEMM) with a novel mixed-precision data layout that co-locates 4-bit and 8-bit activation elements to enable fast dequantization. The kernel uses GPU software pipelining to overlap data loading and conversion with computation, and introduces fine-grained streaming multiprocessor (SM) scheduling to achieve load balance across SMs. COMET integrates this kernel into a full LLM inference framework with efficient KV4 cache management supporting models like LLaMA-3-70B on a single A100-80G.
